title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's 1986 attempt (Analysis situs, première mouture) to axiomatize a 'tame' geometry of figures. There is a set \mathcal F of figures (polyhedra, stratified or semi-analytic sets and the like) with a least element \emptyset_{\mathcal F}. It carries several order relations: \leq (sub-figure), \lesssim (F' is a subdivision of F, i.e. a refinement with the same underlying 'space'), and \ll (F' \ll F iff F' \leq \bar F \lesssim F for some subdivision \bar F of F, as the next page uses: F' is a piece of some subdivision of F). It also has Sup and Inf (\cap) for \leq, and restriction F'|G of a subdivision F' of F to a sub-figure G \leq F.

The page opens by listing two items to add to the axiom list begun on p.85: an axiom for gluing subdivisions, and a package of disjunction axioms.

C8 (axiom of gluing of subdivisions). Suppose:
- F = Sup_i F_i;
- F'_i is a subdivision of F_i for each i;
- the F'_i agree on overlaps: F'_i | (F_i \cap F_j) = F'_j | (F_i \cap F_j).
Then F' = Sup_i F'_i exists and is a subdivision of F. Grothendieck notes it should come right after C6 and replace C6(c).

Corollary: if F = \coprod F_i (a disjoint Sup), then Subdiv(F) \simeq \prod_i Subdiv(F_i). In modern terms, F \mapsto Subdiv(F), with restriction maps, satisfies the existence half of a sheaf condition on the poset of figures, with covering families given by Sup. The disjoint-union case gives the product formula; the uniqueness half is presumably C6.

The second part opens 'Axiomes de disjonction et de support'. To state these axioms as strongly as possible he must first introduce 'les lieux' (points). A crossed-out Proposition/Definition compares, for F \neq \emptyset:
- (a) F is minimal for \leq;
- (b) F is minimal among non-empty figures for \ll.
It also notes this forces F to lie in a subclass \mathcal M and be minimal there. On p.87 this becomes the definition: a lieu is a non-empty figure minimal for \ll. The set of lieux is \mathcal L, and the 'ombre' (shadow, i.e. support) of F is |F| = {x \in \mathcal L : x \ll F}.

So points are not primitive. They are recovered from the poset of figures as minimal non-empty elements under 'is a piece of a subdivision of', and every figure acquires a point-set support. The problem served is a point-free, purely order-theoretic foundation for tame (moderate) topology, as envisaged in Esquisse §5.
errors: The Corollary does not follow from C8 alone. C8 gives existence of a glued subdivision, i.e. surjectivity of Subdiv(F) \to \prod Subdiv(F_i). Injectivity (a subdivision is determined by its restrictions) needs a separate uniqueness statement, presumably the part of C6 that C8 does not replace.

C8 tacitly assumes that the Inf F_i \cap F_j exists and that restriction of subdivisions to sub-figures is defined. In the disjoint case it also needs restriction to \emptyset to be trivial, so that compatibility is vacuous. None of these is stated on this page.

The crossed-out equivalence a)<=>b): the proof on p.87 also gets struck through, and Grothendieck himself notes the converse (minimal in \mathcal M for \leq implies lieu) is not provable from the axioms so far. The proposition was withdrawn and replaced by a definition.

ideas.what: Axiom C8: subdivisions defined compatibly on the members of a Sup-covering glue uniquely to a subdivision of the Sup; corollary Subdiv(\coprod F_i) = \prod Subdiv(F_i)
ideas.modern_name: sheaf/descent condition for the presheaf of subdivisions (refinements, triangulations) on a poset of tame sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology and stratification theory (gluing of triangulations and refinements); no axiomatic source
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 motivates tame topology but contains no such axiom

ideas.what: Points ('lieux') defined as minimal non-empty figures for the relation \ll (piece of a subdivision); support ('ombre') |F| = set of lieux \ll F
ideas.modern_name: point-free topology: recovering points from a lattice of regions (atoms, minimal elements); support maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone, Wallman, Ehresmann, Isbell (locales); Whitehead/Tarski in mereotopology

ideas.what: Plan to split the axioms into formal axioms for \leq alone, formal compatibilities between \leq and \lesssim, and separate 'disjonction et support' axioms
ideas.modern_name: axiomatics of tame topology / o-minimal-like structures via order relations on figures
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Shiota (o-minimal and semialgebraic axiomatics), from a set-theoretic rather than order-theoretic starting point

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a point-free axiomatization of tame topology. Figures carry sub-figure, subdivision and 'piece of a subdivision' orders, subdivisions form a sheaf for Sup-coverings (C8), and points emerge as \ll-minimal non-empty figures with supports |F|. This order-theoretic programme for the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse seems never to have been developed in print. Existing approaches (o-minimality, definable sets) take a point set as primitive.
missed.quote: Pour formuler les axiomes sous forme aussi forte et commode que possible, c'est le moment d'introduire les lieux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a mereotopological/locale-style foundation for tame geometry in which subdivisions (triangulations, stratification refinements) are primary data with a sheaf property. This could connect o-minimal triangulation theory with point-free topology and with stratified/exit-path frameworks.

missed.claim: C8 makes subdivision a sheaf on the lattice of figures. Together with the reconstruction of points as minimal elements, this implicitly links refinement theory to locale/Grothendieck-topology ideas: Sup-covers act as a coverage on the poset of figures.
missed.quote: alors F' = Sup F'_i existe et est une subdivision de F ... Subdiv(F) \simeq \prod_i Subdiv(F_i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Treating 'the stack of subdivisions' as a sheaf on a site of tame figures is a natural framework for refinement-invariant constructions (combinatorial invariants, constructible sheaves). It is not formulated this way in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The gluing axiom itself is routine. The page is a fragment of an unpublished, order-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology with points derived rather than primitive, which is a notable but sketchy unpublished direction.
transcription_corrections: 'c'est le moment d'introduire ces liens' should read 'c'est le moment d'introduire les lieux' (points), consistent with the definition of 'lieu' on p.87.
'aussi forte et sensible que possible' is more likely 'aussi forte et commode que possible' (reading uncertain).
Second header line: '[Un] paquet d'axiomes de disjonction' – 'paquet' reading is plausible; 'Un' is struck through.
'(Devrait suivre C6), et remplace C6 (c)' is probably '(Devrait suivre C6), cela remplace C6 (c)'.
In the crossed-out definition, condition a) may use \lesssim/\preceq rather than \leq ('F' \lesssim F \Rightarrow F' = F'); the reading is unclear from the image.
